Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a landscape 3:2 art-direction concept board for NATHANIEL, an original isometric RTS set on futuristic Earth years after an alien invasion. This is visual exploration, not finished game assets.
Text: top left, a modest clean label exactly "A / IRON & INK". No other lettering, no logos.
Scene: a small square patch of dry post-apocalyptic woodland, isolated on a warm light grey background, viewed as a broad 2:1 diamond. Thin ground edge, not a thick floating island. One worn pale path crosses diagonally from screen lower-left to upper-right. Exactly one Nathaniel stands on the path just left of center; one Hermes stands beside him right of center; one defensive gun tower stands behind the two units towards upper-center. Two sparse trees are on the far left and far right edges, and two clusters of three chunky rocks sit near the front-left and rear-right edges. Keep terrain sparse, uncluttered and low contrast, with ample clear space around all units.
Camera invariant: orthographic isometric game view, 45-degree azimuth, 30-degree elevation above ground, no perspective convergence, verticals upright. Entire scene visible, static gameplay composition, no horizon. Ground diamond roughly from x=10% to90%, y=30% to88%. Nathaniel about 11% of total image height. Hermes about 13% image height and 1.7 times Nathaniel's width. Tower about 20% image height. All units face screen lower-left, three-quarter front views, fully visible and separated.
Direction A: gritty British science-fiction comic energy, bold black outer contour lines and decisive cel-shaded masses, muted petrol-blue machinery, ochre identification panels, bone-grey ground, very restrained rust-red wear. Angular chunky silhouettes, dramatic design but even readable daylight, hard graphic shadow shapes, NOT dramatic atmospheric lighting. Original designs only, no existing comic character costumes or insignia.
Nathaniel: recognizably a HUMAN MAN inside heavy angular armor, small exposed human face in open helmet, broad squared shoulders, heavy boots, narrow waist, ochre shoulder plate, holding a compact squared rifle low. No spikes, cape or elaborate ornament.
Hermes: broad box-shaped industrial bipedal robot, squat torso, tiny recessed sensor head, large simple forearms, one broad clamp hand, chest matter-intake hatch shaped like a dark rectangular industrial furnace opening; closed safe idle mode, no gore. Feels like a powerful builder made by Nathaniel's father, not another armored soldier. A small flat amber intake indicator, no glow haze.
Tower: square prefabricated pedestal with four short outriggers and a single compact cannon, clearly the same manufactured blue-and-ochre family as Hermes. Three or four major modular shapes, almost no surface greebles.
Trees: simple crooked low-poly trunks and 3-4 broad angular olive leaf clumps. Rocks: grey faceted primitives. Dead branches and cracked soil communicate the apocalypse without clutter.
Rendering constraint: look achievable by one developer using simple bevelled cubes, cylinders and low-poly trees in Blender rendered into crisp sprites. Maximum 3 tones per material, flat colors, coarse painted wear only, no intricate illustration hatching, no hundreds of bolts, no photoreal textures. Every important identifying feature survives a reduction to around 72 pixels unit height. Units must have markedly stronger value contrast than background props.
Avoid: UI, HUD, selection circles, speech bubbles, action poses, motion blur, bloom, fog, smoke, film grain, depth of field, cinematic effects, realistic foliage, skyline or buildings, giant hero portrait, additional characters.

Use case: stylized-concept. New concept-art sheet for the original isometric RTS NATHANIEL. Input image is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: follow its IRON & INK style closely, but create the new subjects and sheet layout below. Gritty science-fiction comic feel; angular low-poly forms, decisive black outer contours, 2-3 cel-shaded values per material, flat patches of coarse wear. Achievable as simple bevelled cubes, low-poly shells, cylinders and wedges in Blender rendered to sprites. NO intricate sculpting, fine greebles, dense scratches, filigree, hundreds of bolts, or microtextures. Broad readable shapes must work around 72px unit height. Restrained upper-left daylight with crisp contact shadows, no fog, bloom, atmospheric effects, action, or gore. Every subject in the same orthographic isometric view, 45 degree azimuth /30 degree elevation, three-quarter fronts facing screen lower-left; verticals upright, no perspective convergence. Landscape 3:2 board on warm off-white neutral background, modest clean dark sans-serif title at top left. Lots of breathing room, full subjects visible and never overlapping labels. Concept sheet only, no UI, HUD, decorative border, selection circles, gameplay screenshots, extra text or logos.
Title exactly "IRON & INK / ALIEN ENEMIES".
Four concept cells in a balanced 2x2 grid, simple labels directly below each. The first three are living alien attackers, last one demonstrates the matter resource. Aliens must feel from one original invading species, visually unlike the blue and ochre human machines in the reference. Alien design language: matte dark aubergine overlapping broad carapace plates, pale warm grey cutting edges, dark near-black joints, small acid-green vent slits and recessed weapon apertures. Green occupies less than 10% of each body; no glow haze. Each model about 8-12 major masses, short solid limbs, very few joints, no antenna forests or thin spikes. No recognisable franchise creature designs.
Top-left label "GRUNT": small low wide ranged skirmisher, 4 short splayed wedge legs around a compact flattened crab-like torso, one blunt shield-shaped head, a single short biological blaster aperture centered below its face, head and gun mouth do not resemble a human gun barrel. Distinct low horizontal silhouette, 1/2 soldier height but comparable width. Strongly simple chunky shape, no tiny insect feet.
Top-right label "SOLDIER": upright alien 2-legged gunner, reverse-kneed but heavy planted feet, tall angular shell torso and small head sunk below a broad collar. One huge asymmetric forearm is a thick integrated short organic blaster with an acid-green interior, other arm is a simple short claw. Silhouette narrower and taller than grunt, unmistakably an alien rather than armored human.
Bottom-left label "BOSS": very broad squat four-legged siege beast, shell forms one large broken shield crest, not a spiky head crown; paired thick forward weapon lobes beside a tiny recessed face. Large front carapace, low rear abdomen, great solid weight. About 1.25 soldier height and 1.7 soldier width, NOT a building-sized monster. Same material language and repeated simple plates, one unmistakeable central triangular pale crest shape.
Bottom-right label "SOLDIER / SPENT MATTER": same soldier collapsed on its side, legs folded and shell broken into only 2-3 large readable fragments attached to the body. Acid-green slit goes dark, no blood, no organs or gore. One broad exposed dull green inner mass hints at matter that Hermes could reclaim. This cell must look like the dead form of the soldier in the top-right, not a different creature.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Create one NEW art-direction scene for the original isometric RTS NATHANIEL in the selected IRON & INK style. Input 1 is the canonical mobile Hermes design and overall style reference; input 2 is the canonical tower design reference. Preserve the blue-black metal, ochre armor panels, square sensor head with two small amber eyes, rectangular chest matter-intake hatch, black ink contours, and coarse 2-3-tone cel shading. A solo developer must be able to build these forms from simple bevelled boxes, cylinders and hinged rigid plates in Blender and render sprites. Sparse coarse wear, no fine greebles.
Text: modest upper-left title exactly "IRON & INK / HERMES ANCHOR BASE". Small subtitle immediately below exactly "DEPLOYED / STATIONARY / ARMED". No other text.
Main subject: Hermes has transformed INTO a low field base. He must not be a normal standing robot next to a separate base. Torso lowers, knees fold completely under the body, lower armor unfolds into four very short broad stabilizer legs with massive ground-clamping feet. Deployed body is roughly twice his mobile width and two-thirds his mobile height, mechanically plausible without appearing to gain huge mass. His familiar box sensor head remains on top and his rectangular chest intake remains visible on the front. Blue and ochre shoulder shells hinge outward exposing connection sockets along the lower edges. His right forearm folds up and locks into a short thick single-barrel defense cannon on a swivel bracket above and behind the sensor head, silhouetted clearly, aiming upper-right. Left manipulator folds into side of central fabrication body. No humanoid arms dangling at sides. He reads as a wide anchored robot foundry with recognizable original head and chest, not a bunker or a pile of equipment. Cannon can aim while anchors stay planted.
Scene layout: clear uncluttered small patch of ash-brown earth in an isolated 2:1 isometric ground diamond on warm grey background. Fixed orthographic view,45-degree azimuth,30-degree elevation,upper-left even daylight,no perspective convergence. Hermes at screen center-left. Three distinct towers surround him with ample visible ground between: gun tower upper-right,laser tower lower-right,heal tower lower-left. Faithfully use the three tower designs in input2, shared base and feet. All towers about equal size. Hermes deployed torso slightly lower than tower heads but much wider than a tower base. Ground includes only 2-3 large faint cracks and one small rock cluster near edge, no trees, grass or terrain noise masking links.
CRITICAL connections: each tower has ONE distinct thick physical armored ground conduit directly to a separate socket on Hermes. Exactly THREE conduits,total,one per tower. All endpoints are visibly attached at both ends: an ochre socket on Hermes and an ochre socket low on the inward-facing side of each tower plinth. Link routes fully visible on bare ground; no route crossings, no part hidden behind Hermes, no free-floating loose ends. Use flat flexible cable-carrier/conduit geometry, narrow segmented rectangular dark-steel sections with a broad intermittent ochre center stripe and black outlines. Each link about one-fifth the width of a tower pedestal, clearly narrower than a walkway or bridge. Conduits lie flush along ground with gentle simple bends and a tiny contact shadow. Connections are physical matter-transfer tethers, not lasers, forcefields, glowing power lines or UI overlays.
Communication: stillness, solidity, linked temporary camp. All four anchors planted and locked. Hermes visibly armed but not firing. No other characters. Entire scene visible in landscape3:2 composition, generous margin, objects comfortably separated and silhouettes readable at game scale. No holograms, active beams, UI, selection circles, motion blur, dust, smoke, magical effects, bloom, cinematic lighting, technical arrows or exploded parts. This is concept illustration,not a finished production render.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a clear SIX-PANEL visual storyboard showing the complete deploy-build-recycle cycle of Hermes for original isometric RTS NATHANIEL. Landscape3:2 canvas, generous clean warm-grey background, two rows of three equal panels, very subtle separators and large simple illustrations. Every panel same orthographic isometric camera:45-degree azimuth/30-degree elevation. Same camera scale, identical character identity, similar placement in each panel, top-left even light, hard cel-shaded masses and bold dark contours.
REFERENCE1: canonical mobile robot Hermes, the blue and ochre boxy biped on the right of the scene. Ignore Nathaniel and environment. Preserve Hermes's square sensor head with two amber eyes, large chest intake, shoulder shells, heavy feet and simple forearms.
REFERENCE2: canonical deployed Hermes low anchor-base shape and physical links. Match this design precisely in deployed panels, including same head, chest intake, four short deployed stabilizer legs, above-body short cannon, and blue/ochre armor. Copy the gun tower and thick segmented ground conduit. Ignore extra towers and setting; this storyboard uses just ONE representative connected gun tower to make the cycle legible. Last frame has no base elements left.
Title in top margin exactly "IRON & INK / DEPLOY AND RECYCLE".
Panel labels below illustrations exactly as follows, no other text:
Top-left "1 / MOBILE": Hermes in canonical original standing biped mode, fully visible, no tower, no conduits, no separate platform or pads. Hands down, cannon mechanism folded flush inside shoulder/forearm mass. Sole subject.
Top-middle "2 / LOCK DOWN": same robot halfway transforming in place; knees retract under torso, large foot plates slide outward into four anchored supports, shoulders open, right arm folded up into swivel cannon. Head and chest stay recognizable. No tower and no link yet. Show ONE short unobtrusive dark curved arrow for a folding part if useful, no floating spare parts. It is a mechanical transformation, not a new building growing over him.
Top-right "3 / FABRICATE": Hermes fully in canonical anchored base mode at center-left of cell, armed gun raised, ONE attached armored segmented ground conduit curves to screen right and ends at a clearly attached ochre tower socket. At far end a gun tower is half built: fixed four-foot plinth complete, pedestal partially rising, gun head still a compact folded module atop it. TWO small flat amber travelling markers inside conduit top seams point OUTWARD from Hermes to tower. No beam, construction crane, worker or unrelated props.
Bottom-left "4 / HOLD": Hermes fully anchored as in ref2, gun turned toward screen upper-left, one completely assembled reference gun tower to his screen right, one continuous attached ground conduit between sockets. Strong still grounded posture; no wheels or moving feet. No firing, explosion or targets.
Bottom-middle "5 / RECLAIM": keep Hermes locked down. Same tower to right now folds inward: gun head folded against lowered telescoping pedestal, four-foot base half retracted; show compact folded tower about half previous height, not rubble or explosion. The conduit remains attached at both ends. TWO flat amber travelling markers inside conduit seams now point BACK TOWARD Hermes. A small simple dark arrow adjacent to link may clarify inward direction. Matter returns along the same physical link; no loose chunks flying through air and no holographic dissolving. Connection disappears only after tower is gone.
Bottom-right "6 / MOVE OUT": Hermes returned exactly to standing original biped, same head chest armor and limbs as panel1, one foot taking a small walking step. ALL tower and base parts have been reclaimed: NO plinth,NO foundation,NO cable,NO separate pad,NO scrap,NO companion structure remains anywhere in this panel. Only Hermes and a soft contact shadow. Closed chest intake and folded cannon.
Rendering: match chosen Iron & Ink comic-tech style, petrol blue and ochre, 2-3 values per material, simple low-poly bevelled boxes and cylinders. Plain quiet ground only directly under objects, no textured terrain islands, stones, vegetation, towers in backgrounds, extra robots, UI, captions beyond specified labels, glowing effects, smoke, dust, motion blur or fine mechanical greebles. All panels large and readable, each object safely within its panel, labels well separated. Concept board, not game UI.

Create new environment concept art for the original isometric RTS NATHANIEL. Input image is a STYLE AND SETTING REFERENCE ONLY: use the IRON & INK bold black contours, angular simple Blender-model forms, matte cel shading, warm sandy post-apocalyptic earth and quiet worn colors. Do not copy its robot, man, tower or any science-fiction machine.
The requested subjects are ORDINARY RECOGNIZABLE EARTH BUILDINGS in a dry sandy almost-desert area, abandoned and disheveled years after an invasion. Contemporary mundane architecture, simple functional shapes, absolutely no futuristic turrets, robotic modules, alien shapes, medieval fantasy forms, spaceship parts, giant glowing vents or military faction color coding. Sand-stained faded plaster, weathered brick, charcoal metal and restrained terracotta/rust roof surfaces. Title exactly "IRON & INK / EARTH BUILDINGS 01".
Top row labels both exactly "HOUSE". A normal modest one-storey detached Earth house: faded sand-colored stucco over block walls, low shallow-sloping terracotta tile roof represented by 4-5 broad roof strips rather than individual tiles, a small box chimney near back-left, one front doorway beneath a shallow porch canopy, a pair of simple rectangular windows, one short side extension. Weathered version has a missing patch at a roof corner, one boarded window, peeling plaster in 3 broad patches, and windblown sand along lower walls. House remains structurally standing. Destroyed version loses central roof and rear-right wall, leaving a broken front facade, chimney stump, clear same doorway and porch posts, side extension corner, and a few chunky roof slabs. No toilet, kitchen or furniture interior.
Bottom row labels both exactly "CORNER SHOP". Small one-storey flat-roof brick/stucco corner shop: broad glass storefront below a faded dark teal metal awning, recessed single entrance at one end, cream parapet with a wide BLANK faded sign rectangle above shopfront. No legible shop branding or extra lettering. Window panes are flat dark panels with 1-2 large broken silhouettes, not fine glass detail. Small higher storage room at rear creates an L-shaped roof outline. Weathered version has crooked awning edge, boarded portion of shopfront, broad dirty plaster and cracked paving. Destroyed version has roof and most rear room collapsed inward, awning bent into 2 broad slabs, front doorway jamb and one shopfront corner still standing, same surviving blank sign/parapet fragment. Large legible slabs of roof and wall occupy original foundation. Keep sand and wear muted so the building silhouettes dominate.
